newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded prices firm in Chicago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded prices firm in Chicago.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline prices firmed on Wednesday as firming differentials more than offset the drop in NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures on the day, traders said.
Chicago prompt unleaded barrels began trading at a premium to the print for the first time this season, and Group Three unleaded basis continued to draw nearer the print.
Unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel drew support in the spot Chicago and Group Three markets from draws reported in the weekly American Petroleum Institite stocks report, traders said.
Midwest refineries reported 28.1 million barrels of distillate inventories on hand in the PADD 2 region, a 912,000 barrel draw on the week, API said late Tuesday.
Gasoline stocks on hand at Midwest refineries were pegged at 53.12 million barrels, down 1.46 million barrels on the week, API said.
Chicago unleaded gasoline for prompt April deliveries was bid 0.25 cent a gallon over NYMEX May unleaded, with later deliveries bid 0.25 cent below the print.
Group Three unleaded was bid 1.0 cent a gallon under the print for all April timings.
Low sulphur diesel for April deliveries was talked 4.0/4.25 cents a gallon over NYMEX May heating oil in Chicago and 5.75/6.0 cents over in Group Three, traders said.
High sulphur was talked 2.0/2.25 cents a gallon over the print in both Midwest markets.
